report: Checked all seven candidate lemmas; none is a split. Every difference is one the ASV writes: the 2ms suffix takes thee where it is the object of a verb or participle (v3 keepeth thee, v6 smite thee, v7 keep thee) and thy where it is possessive (v5 thy keeper, thy shade, thy right hand; v7 thy soul; v8 thy going out, thy coming in).

שָׁמַר construct participle: v3 and v4 both take the supplied he that with the participle under rule 46, headed on keepeth, and v5 takes is keeper because the ASV writes it as a predicate noun there (rule 20). The three finite forms all keep auxiliary plus lexical verb headed on keep. Consistent.

Negation and waw: v4 gives neither to the first written לֹא and fuses וְלֹא into nor headed on the negative (rules 14, 35); v6 gives Nor to a bare waw over a colon whose negative is gapped (rules 25, 35). Both are what the source licenses.

Articles, לְ and בּוֹא differ only by ASV rendering (of Ascents vs to be moved; going out / coming in vs shall come). v8's מֵעַתָּה וְעַד־עוֹלָם matches rule 26's own example exactly (and to the waw, for to עַד, evermore to עוֹלָם).
v2's cometh placed on מֵעִם as a linking verb under rules 20/49 is defensible and its note names the competing added reading; left as accepted.
BSB: 79/79 agree, nothing to adjudicate. No conventions, promotions or amendments: nothing here goes beyond what the contract already states.
